question: Which of the following statements accurately describes the relationship between UI Policies and Client Scripts regarding form performance?

choices.text: UI Policies and Client Scripts have identical execution times, so the choice between them is purely a matter of personal preference.
Client Scripts are always faster than UI Policies because they execute directly in the browser without framework overhead.
UI Policies should be used whenever possible instead of Client Scripts because they are optimized for faster load times.
UI Policies execute on the server, while Client Scripts execute on the client, making UI Policies slower for form manipulation.

explanation: ServiceNow documentation explicitly states that while both UI Policies and Client Scripts can perform similar actions (like making fields mandatory or read-only), UI Policies are preferred for faster load times and better performance when scripting is not strictly necessary.
pieges: Confusing the execution environment of UI Policies (client-side) with server-side rules.
Assuming Client Scripts are always the more performant option for developers.
